Introduction

Dataset

diabetes dataset from package VIM: a synthetic replacement for the Pima Indians Diabetes data

  • Data about diabetes on females at least 21 years old of Pima Indian heritage.
  • One column removed (DiabetesPedigreeFunction).
Code 
library(VIM)
pa_data <- diabetes[-7]
levels(pa_data$Outcome) <- c("No diabetes", "Diabetes")

Useful packages for documenting missing data

  • Base R functions

  • Tools from the tidyverse suite

  • Dedicated packages, among which:

    • naniar (see https://naniar.njtierney.com/)
    • VIM
Code 
pacman::p_load(c(naniar, VIM))

Documenting missing data

Visualization above: a good glimpse of the data.

Here: more specific summary statistics and visualizations to explore the patterns and mechanisms of missing data.

Overview of missingness

Data overview

Code 
visdat::vis_miss(pa_data) + # naniar::vis_miss(pa_data) # equivalent
  theme(axis.text.x.top = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0))

  • For reasonably small datasets: very informative.

  • For larger datasets: may not fit on the screen and be less useful \(\Rightarrow\) need summaries.

Missingness by variable

Code 
naniar::gg_miss_var(pa_data) +
  ggtitle("Number of Missing Values per variable")
Code 
naniar::gg_miss_var(pa_data, show_pct = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Percentage of Missing Values per variable")

Missingness by case

Code 
naniar::miss_case_table(pa_data) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_label(
    n_miss_in_case ~ "# missing variable in case",
    n_cases = "N cases",
    pct_cases = "% cases"
  )
# missing variable in case N cases % cases
0 362 47.135417
1 147 19.140625
2 227 29.557292
3 20 2.604167
4 12 1.562500

Co-missingness (missingness patterns)

Investigate if some variables are systematically or more frequently missing in the same cases.

Code 
naniar::gg_miss_upset(pa_data)

Insulin and Skin Thickness very often missing at the same time.

Code 
plot(VIM::aggr(pa_data), combined = TRUE, cex.axis = 0.7)

Link between missingness and other variables

Overview of missingness by category of a factor

  • Visualize the missing status of each cell for each diabetes status.

  • To check whether the proportion of missing values in a variable seems to be associated with the diabetes status.

Code 
naniar::vis_miss(pa_data, facet = Outcome) +
  theme(axis.text.x.top = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0))
  • No obvious link between diabetes status and proportion of missingness in other variables.

Data overview by sorting on a variable

  • Visualization of the whole dataset (missing values and observed values).
  • By sorting the rows by one variable, we can investigate whether the missingness in the other variables seems to be associated with this variable.

Rows sorted by Age.

Beware: here,

  • black cells are observed values
  • red cells are missing values
Code 
VIM::matrixplot(pa_data[,-1], sortby = "Age", cex.axis = 0.7)
  • Missing values in Blood Pressure and BMI seem more frequent for young people.

Rows sorted by Glucose.

Code 
VIM::matrixplot(pa_data[,-1], sortby = "Glucose", cex.axis = 0.7)
  • No obvious trend between Glucose level and missingness in other variables.

Rows sorted by diabetes status.

Code 
VIM::matrixplot(pa_data[,-1], sortby = "Outcome", cex.axis = 0.7)

Bivariate tools

Classical tools

Proportion of missing Insulin for each diabetes status

Code 
round(prop.table(table(pa_data$Outcome, is.na(pa_data$Insulin)), margin = 1),2)
             
              FALSE TRUE
  No diabetes  0.50 0.50
  Diabetes     0.43 0.57
  • Missingness in Insulin seems more frequent for patients with diabetes than for patients without diabetes.

Distribution of Pregnancies for patients with missing Insulin vs. patients with observed Insulin values

Code 
boxplot(Pregnancies ~ is.na(Insulin), data = pa_data)
  • Patients with missing Insulin values tend to have more pregnancies than patients with observed Insulin values.

Tools dedicated to missing values

Visualize:

  • the relationship between two variables (will be useful for multiple imputation).
  • the relationship between the missingness in one of them and the observed values of the other one.
Code 
pa_data |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = Age, y = BloodPressure) +
  naniar::geom_miss_point(alpha = 1)
Code 
VIM::marginplot(pa_data[c("Age","BloodPressure")], cex.axis = 1)
  • Link between Age and missingness in Blood Pressure: missing values in Blood Pressure are more frequent for young people.
  • Dispersion of Age is larger for cases with no missing value in BloodPressure.
Code 
VIM::marginplot(pa_data[c("BMI","Insulin")], cex.axis = 1)
  • Patients with missing values in Insulin tend to have a lower BMI than patients with observed values in Insulin.
